StackType.rationale: ThieveryPower.cs:15 PowerStackType.Counter, and the sim's inherited on_stack adds unconditionally, matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citation, not hashed.

InstanceType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): ThieveryPower.instance_type = PowerInstanceType.INSTANCED (sts2_rl/powers.py), mirroring ThieveryPower.cs:17. Verified directly by test/test_powers.py::TestPowerInstanceType::test_thievery_two_applications_are_independent_gold_counters. DORMANT stands: the only applier (GremlinMerc.AfterAddedToRoom) applies it once per Merc.  The text it replaced read: ThieveryPower.cs:17 PowerInstanceType.Instanced, which the sim's single-slot target.powers dict (cmds.py:310-326, keyed on power_cls.id) cannot represent -- the mechanism owned by audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json G5, cross-referenced not re-verdicted. DORMANT for this unit: the only applier is GremlinMerc.AfterAddedToRoom applying it once to itself (monsters/underdocks/gremlin_merc.py:40, one Merc per encounter, re-verified 2026-08-04 -- line renumbered from :37-39), so a second simultaneous instance is not reachable. NOTE FOR THE STREAM REPORT: this is a TENTH PowerInstanceType unit, absent from section 10 item 3's list of nine purely because it was absent from the roster.

Steal() -- public, NOT public override.rationale: Recorded so a reader does not think it was skipped: ThieveryPower.cs:21 is a plain public method, not a hook, so harness.list_overrides correctly does not enumerate it (the same shape as CrueltyPower.ModifyVulnerableMultiplier). Its caller is the Merc's move. The port is faithful in both arithmetic and guard: C# takes Math.Min(Amount, Target.Player.Gold) (:25) and the sim takes min(self.amount, available) (powers.py:2152) where available is player_gold + gold_gained - gold_stolen (powers.py:2151) -- equivalent because C# mutates player.Gold immediately (PlayerCmd.cs:198) so a second Steal reads the reduced figure, exactly as the sim's running gold_stolen debit does. C#'s Gold > 0 test (:23) and the sim's amount <= 0 early return (powers.py:2153) agree because Amount is a positive 20. Citations re-verified and renumbered 2026-08-04 (steal() now at powers.py:2146-2156).

guards.what: ThieveryPower.cs:26 PlayerCmd.LoseGold(GoldLossType.Stolen) vs the sim's deferred debit
guards.rationale: EXECUTED READ of the command rather than assumed: PlayerCmd.LoseGold (PlayerCmd.cs:178-199) fires NO hooks at all -- it writes three history counters, calls MarkLootStolen, and assigns player.Gold. So the sim accumulating combat.gold_stolen and settling in RunState.finish_combat is observationally identical for every ported listener, because there are no listeners to observe. This is the reason the divergence is faithful rather than deliberate: had LoseGold dispatched a hook, the deferral would be a gap.

guards.what: ThieveryPower.cs:23 base.Target vs the sim's combat.player
guards.rationale: C# guards base.Target != null && !base.Target.IsDead and reads base.Target.Player.Gold; the sim reads combat.player.is_dead and combat.player_gold (powers.py:2149-2151). Identical in single-player, which is the only scope -- multiplayer is out of scope by the shared audit contract's Global scope section. Flagged rather than waived because it is the sim resolving an identity, not skipping a feature. Citation renumbered 2026-08-04.

C# accumulates the running total into a DynamicVar so the power's description can render it; the sim keeps the same total in a plain attribute (powers.py:2144, 2156) which SurprisePower then reads to size the Fat Gremlin's HeistPower. Same value, and the DynamicVar machinery itself is presentation. Waiver. Citation renumbered 2026-08-04.
